tools.name: create_inbox
tools.description: Create a new disposable email inbox. Returns its address, password and a token for the other tools. Inboxes are receive-only and are kept until deleted. Save the address and password: tokens expire, and login_inbox gets a new one.

tools.name: login_inbox
tools.description: Get a fresh token for an existing inbox (tokens expire; inboxes don't).

tools.name: wait_for_email
tools.description: Wait for unread email in an inbox and return it, including extracted one-time codes and verification links. Returns immediately if unread mail exists. Each message is returned once; it is marked read afterwards.

tools.name: list_emails
tools.description: List the most recent emails in an inbox (newest first), with codes, without full bodies.

tools.name: read_email
tools.description: Read one email in full: plain text, codes, links and attachment names.

tools.name: delete_inbox
tools.description: Delete an inbox and all of its email immediately.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_inbox" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp?ref=mcp-registry" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_inbox, login_inbox, wait_for_email, list_emails, read_email · Private data: create_inbox, login_inbox · Public sink: create_inbox, wait_for_email, read_email, delete_inbox · Destructive: delete_inbox.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_inbox, login_inbox, wait_for_email, list_emails, read_email · Private data: create_inbox, login_inbox · Public sink: create_inbox, wait_for_email, read_email, delete_inbox · Destructive: delete_inbox

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
